content: 1. Do not rely solely on hormonal contraception when taking lesinurad, as it may not provide adequate contraceptive protection. 2. Leteormovir increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Ethinylestradiol reduces the efficacy of letrozole due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 4. Letrozole should not be co-administered with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 5. Levofloxacin decreases ethinylestradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Levoketoconazole increases ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Levoketoconazole also increases norethindrone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, but the clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 8. Ethinylestradiol reduces liraglutide efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 10. Lixisenatide decreases ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 11. GLP-1 agonists delay gastric emptying, potentially affecting the absorption of oral medications. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least 1 hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. 12. Ethinylestradiol increases lomitapide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lomitapide doses should not exceed 30 mg/day. 13. Ethinylestradiol increases lonafarnib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative medications. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce lonafarnib to its starting dose and monitor for arrhythmias and QT interval changes. 14. Ethinylestradiol reduces lonapegsomatropin efficacy by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral estrogens may reduce serum IGF-1 response to growth hormone analogs, necessitating higher growth hormone doses. Monitor closely. 15. Lopinavir increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 16. Lopinavir increases ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative medications. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, reducing hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Use nonhormonal contraception. 17. Lorlatinib decreases ethinylestradiol and norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative medications. Monitor response to estrogens and progestins when CYP3A4 inducers are added or discontinued, and adjust hormone dosages as needed. 18. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases norethindrone and ethinylestradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concurrent use unless benefits outweigh risks. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during co-administration. 19. Lumefantrine decreases ethinylestradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Norethindrone increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Mavacamten decreases norethindrone and ethinylestradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 22. Ethinylestradiol decreases metformin efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Metronidazole decreases ethinylestradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Ethinylestradiol decreases metyrapone efficacy through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative medications. Discontinuing estrogens before and during metyrapone administration may be advisable. 25. Ethinylestradiol increases mexiletine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Ethinylestradiol increases midazolam levels by inhibiting metabolism, potentially prolonging sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Mifepristone increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and decreases norethindrone and ethinylestradiol efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 28. Mineral oil decreases ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. The clinical significance is unknown. 29. Minocycline decreases ethinylestradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Mitotane decreases norethindrone and ethinylestradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concurrent use unless benefits outweigh risks. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during co-administration. 31. Momelotinib increases ethinylestradiol toxicity through plasma protein binding competition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 32. Moxifloxacin decreases ethinylestradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Mycophenolate decreases ethinylestradiol efficacy through an unknown mechanism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative contraception. 34. Nafcillin decreases norethindrone and ethinylestradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Nonhormonal contraception is advised during therapy. 35. Ethinylestradiol increases naratriptan effects through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 36. Nefazodone increases ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 37. Nelfinavir increases norethindrone and ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative medications. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, reducing hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Use nonhormonal contraception. 38. Nemolizumab decreases norethindrone and ethinylestradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Dosage adjustments may be necessary. 39. Neomycin decreases ethinylestradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Nevirapine decreases ethinylestradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative contraception. 41. Ethinylestradiol increases nicardipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Ethinylestradiol increases nilotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Nirmatrelvir decreases ethinylestradiol levels by inducing metabolism, possibly through ritonavir-mediated CYP2C9 or CYP1A2 induction. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider additional nonhormonal contraception for the remainder of the cycle. 44. Nitrofurantoin decreases ethinylestradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Ethinylestradiol may increase nortriptyline levels by reducing oxidative metabolism, potentially increasing antidepressant serum concentrations and adverse effects. Monitor closely. 46. Ofloxacin decreases ethinylestradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Ethinylestradiol increases olanzapine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Omaveloxolone decreases ethinylestradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative contraception. 49. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir are contraindicated with ethinylestradiol due to an unspecified interaction mechanism.
